coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Each lateral frame cropped from the full scan at 1.5-2x with a grid labelled in scan pixels; feet zoomed at 3-5x with contrast to judge contact. A foot is 'down' when its sole or toe meets the ground line / its own shadow. Legs are tracked by continuity (the stance foot's position steps back frame by frame within the frame box) and named legA/legB. Joint points (shoulder, hip, knee, ankle, toe tip, elbow, wrist) were read off the grid, drawn back onto the crop as dots and segments, inspected, and corrected or dropped; only kept points are listed. Hip = centre of the upper thigh at greater-trochanter level, shoulder = centre of the humeral head: these two are estimates of hidden landmarks, about +/-15 px, i.e. about +/-5 deg on thigh angles and +/-7 deg on trunk lean in a single frame. Knee, ankle, toe, elbow, wrist about +/-5 px. Hip and shoulder are taken as one point for both sides (side view). Angles computed by atan2 from the kept points only. Timing: catalogue interval; the cycle was checked against observed contacts. Plate frames come from different cameras, so stride length and speed were not measured.

legs.legA: far (shadowed) leg; lands between frames 2 and 3, stance frames 3-6
legs.legB: near (lit) leg; its thigh overlaps the other in frames 5-6 and 2 (medium confidence); lands between frames 8 and 9
legs.arms: 'Fwd'/'Back' = whichever arm is ahead of / behind the shoulder in that frame (the forward arm is the near one in frames 1-3, the far one in 5-8, medium confidence)

angleDefinitions.thigh: knee relative to hip, degrees from vertical, + = knee ahead of the hip (runner faces +x)
angleDefinitions.hipFlex: thigh + trunkLean: thigh relative to the trunk line, + = flexion
angleDefinitions.ankle: unsigned angle knee-ankle-toe tip (larger = more plantarflexed; our figure's standing rest is 116)
angleDefinitions.trunkLean: hip -> shoulder line from vertical, + = forward

timing.cyclesSource: muybridge-1887-catalogue (fraction of a stride shown on the plate)
timing.observed: No foot is seen to land twice (only 10 frames). legA touches down between frames 2-3 and legB between frames 8-9, both with the same pattern (frames 1-2 and 7-8 airborne, front foot descending): a half cycle of 6 intervals (5-7), so a full cycle of about 12 intervals = 0.50 s, assuming left/right symmetry. The plate therefore shows about 9/12 = 0.75 of a cycle, not the catalogue's 5/8; the catalogue cycle (0.605 s) is about 20% longer than observed.

derived.stanceFrom: legA: touchdown in (2,3], toe-off in [6,7) -> 4 intervals (3-5)

derived.supportPattern: single support alternating with flight: a run

comparison: Cycle: plate about 0.50 s (catalogue 0.605 s) vs our run 0.727 s (8 frames at 11 fps): our cycle is 45% longer than this half-mile pace. A slower jog fits ours better; a race-pace run would need about 6 frames at 12 fps.
Duty: plate 0.33 (0.25-0.42) vs ours 0.35: agrees. Flight per step about 0.17 of the cycle vs ours 0.15: agrees.
Thigh: plate -34 to +72 deg from vertical vs ours -6.5 to +57: ours lacks the backward extension at toe-off (about 27 deg short) and about 15 deg of forward knee lift.
Knee: plate swing maximum 145 deg vs ours 109: ours folds the swing leg about 35 deg less. Late-stance minimum 20 vs ours 28: close.

Ankle (knee-ankle-toe): plate 94-164 deg, never below about 94; ours 50-130. Ours dorsiflexes the swing foot far more than the plate (by up to about 45 deg) and plantarflexes less just after toe-off (164 vs 130).
Trunk lean: plate 3-14 deg (mean about 8) vs ours a constant 11.7 (hip-shoulder line): in range.

Arms: plate upper arm -62 to +25 deg vs ours -45 to +19: ours swings about 25 deg less, mostly behind. Elbow: plate's forward arm opens to 19-60 deg, the back arm bends 56-94; ours stays at 88-104 throughout, too bent for the forward arm.

findings: Running at a half-mile gait (shoes): flight in frames 1-2 and 7-8, single support in 3-6 and 9-10. Duty 0.33 and flight per step 0.17 of the cycle.

Observed cycle about 0.50 s (12 frames at 42 ms); the catalogue fraction 5/8 would give 0.605 s. Successive contacts of the same foot are not on the plate, so the cycle rests on two opposite-foot touchdowns 6 intervals apart and left/right symmetry.
The near/far assignment of the legs is medium confidence (from which thigh overlaps the other in frames 2, 5 and 6); the timing results do not depend on it.

Not measured: stride length and speed (each frame is a different camera); the front-view row (10 frames); legA's knee in frames 4 and 10 (hidden behind the other thigh) and legB's in 10; legB's toe in 5; arm points in 4, 9 and 10 (arms overlap the trunk). Hip and shoulder are estimated landmarks (+/-15 px), so single-frame trunk lean is +/-7 deg.
